text:
micah: FYI — during the compliance sprint we noticed ~18 permission-change audit entries with actor:null after last night's auth-service migration. SOC2 report needs author info. Anyone seen this?

jess: looking now. I can repro locally against the migrated DB. timestamps cluster around 2026-03-19T03:11:xxZ. :thinking_face:

rohan: what changed in the migration? was the audit emitter touched?

micah: migration was schema change + move of audit payloads from jsonb->encrypted_blob. migration job did re-encryption with the new KMS key.

jess: aha — some blobs decrypt but others fail with KMS "InvalidCiphertext" in the worker logs. that explains null actor: we parse audit payload after decrypt, fallback to minimal event with no actor when decryption fails.

audit-bot: deploy-log: auth-service-migrate v2 deployed @ 2026-03-19T03:05Z — all instances restarted.

rohan: does key rotation coincide with this? I remember a KMS rotation request yesterday.

micah: yes, ops rotated the key at 02:50Z; the migration used the new key but some older blobs were still tagged with previous key alias. the migration attempted to decrypt with new key only.

jess: quick scan of the migration job:
```sql
-- simplified: find rows where decrypt fails
select id, created_at, payload_meta->>'kms_key' as orig_key
from audit_events
where payload_encrypted is not null
  and try_decrypt(payload_encrypted, 'alias/redwood-new') is null
limit 50;
```

jess: outcomes: ~18 events where decrypt failed -> we emitted minimal event with actor null. The original raw logs still exist on instances for ~48h.

rohan: do we have a fallback to try previous key alias? Could re-run a backfill that attempts both keys.

micah: ops already approved re-run but we need to be careful: re-encrypting with new key twice could be dangerous. Need an ordered plan: 1) grab encrypted blobs to S3 snapshot, 2) attempt decrypt with old key alias + new key as fallback, 3) mark repaired events, 4) run integration tests.

jess: also dug into code — the RBAC refactor last quarter moved role-change emission into a separate process and we lost the synchronous actor context in the queued job. So even after decryption we might not have the actor if job ran async without user context.

rohan: that's a separate bug. Two tracks: a) fix blobs (KMS/backfill), b) patch emitter to carry actor metadata into queue.

sre-oncall: I'll stand up a temporary runbook and coordinate snapshotting. filing ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SEC-1127 (backfill + KMS), assigned to @jess and @micah.

micah: thanks. for compliance we need an audit report showing which events were repaired and the original actor if recovered. also adding a smoke-check to alert if decrypt fallback returns null.

jess: agreed. I'm going to run a selective backfill in staging first, using previous-key alias: `alias/redwood-old`. If that works we'll run prod in off-hours.

rohan: for the emitter fix: small change to the job payload to include `initiator_id`, then update consumer to prefer initiator over parsed actor. I'll draft PR.

micah: timeline? we need patch + prod backfill within 48h for the SOC2 window.

jess: staging backfill starting in ~30m. will post results here. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

audit-bot: ticket update SEC-1127: status -> in_progress; comment: staging backfill started by jess.

micah: thanks all. if decrypt recovery fails for any event we'll mark those in the compliance CSV with reason "unrecoverable KMS ciphertext" and include raw blob snapshot id so auditors can inspect.

jess: staging backfill complete: 18/18 recovered -> actors restored. running verification job now to update audit index.

rohan: PR ready for emitter fix: https://github.com/redwood/auth-service/pull/784 (adds initiator_id to queued payloads). review appreciated.

micah: excellent. once PR merges we do small canary deploy and then prod backfill. keeping SEC-1127 agile notes updated. :thumbsup:
